title: Printable coordinate grid sheet (lesson 53)
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Enlargement and similarity; ratio and proportion; rates
source: Seeded from mathematics/y9 lesson 53 (Printable coordinate grid sheet (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 53: Enlargement with fractional scale factors. To understand how fractional scale factors make shapes smaller and how to enlarge from a centre with a fractional scale factor

model.title: Enlarge the triangle (2, 2), (6, 2), (2, 8) by scale factor ½, centre (0, 0).

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Each vertex moves to half its distance from the origin

model.title: Enlarge P(7, 5) by scale factor ⅓, centre (1, 2).
An object side is 12 cm and its image side is 4 cm. Find the scale factor.

questions.q: Enlarge (8, 4) by scale factor ¼, centre (0, 0).
questions.model: Multiply each coordinate by ¼. 8 × ¼ = 2 and 4 × ¼ = 1: (2, 1).

questions.q: A 9 cm by 5 cm rectangle is enlarged by scale factor ½.
Object 15 cm, image 6 cm: the scale factor?

(a) Enlarge the square (4, 4), (8, 4), (8, 8), (4, 8) by scale factor ½, centre (0, 0). (b) Enlarge the triangle (3, 3), (9, 3), (3, 9) by scale factor ⅓, centre (0, 0). (c) Enlarge (5, 7) by scale factor ½, centre (1, 1). (d) Find the scale factor when 20 cm becomes 5 cm.
questions.model: (a) The centre is the origin, so halve every coordinate: (4, 4) → (2, 2), (8, 4) → (4, 2), and so on. (c) From (1, 1) to (5, 7) is 4 right and 6 up; half is 2 right and 3 up: (3, 4).

questions.q: A model of a 45 m minaret is made with scale factor 1/150. How tall is the model in cm?
An enlargement with scale factor ⅓ maps (6, 9) to (4, 5). Find the centre.
questions.a: (3, 3): from (3, 3) to (6, 9) is (3, 6); × ⅓ gives (1, 2), landing on (4, 5)

questions.q: Scale factor ½ makes a shape:
The scale factor when 10 cm becomes 4 cm
Big question: can an enlargement make a shape smaller?
questions.a: Yes: a scale factor between 0 and 1 multiplies every length by a fraction, so the image is smaller.
